Impulse is the product of a force and the time for which it acts; it equals the change in momentum.
An airbag increases the time over which the passenger’s momentum changes, reducing the average force on the passenger.
Drawing the hands backward increases the time taken to bring the ball’s momentum to zero, reducing the average force on the fielder’s hands.
Momentum is the product of a body’s mass and velocity (p = mv). Newton’s second law states that the force on a body equals the rate of change of its momentum, in the direction of the force.
The impulse is the change in momentum: 0.4[√(2g × 0.8) + √(2g × 1.8)] ≈ 4.0 N s, upward.
